comments.value: Why doesnt this have more up-votes? This is a huge issue!

A feature that keeps track of avatar audio and auto mutes it if the avatar is a certain radius away or the audio goes on longer than ~5 seconds would also be nice. I like leaving avatar audio on but I don't wanna hear the full soundtrack of your million poly JoJo's Bizarre Adventure avatar.

While we're at it, avatars should NEVER be able to hijack a player's view unless the avatar doing that to you is the one you're wearing (e.g. an avatar with a HUD). I think we can all agree on that and the only avatars I've seen use that are obnoxious memes that zoom your screen in on the meme avatar and whatnot, which is very very very disorientating in VR but happens in public lobbies to new and experienced users alike all the time.

@{5cfb491476b5b77800e860ec|full_name} As long as people can write custom shaders, preventing full screen effects is kind of impossible - at least without severely harming shader capabilities.

There are also legitimate cool use cases for them, such as grenade blast waves that distort the environment, or trippy effects that kick in after you eat a candy from someone's avatar.

@{5cfb491476b5b77800e860ec|full_name} [Community Guidelines](https://hello.vrchat.com/community-guidelines) prohibit disrupting public instances with provocative behavior.

[Creator Guidelines](https://hello.vrchat.com/creator-guidelines) says "Content should not be built or used to disrupt any experience or usage of VRChat.", including "full-screen shaders, full-world audio, excessively large character models, visually disruptive animations, etc", with the caveat that "Exceptions to this category may be made if all users present consent, like for a show or performance."

You can request moderation on bad actors by reporting them. There's also tools at disposal, such as custom Safety Shield settings. Whether that will solve VRChat's optics for new user experience/onboarding or not is debatable, but also off-topic for this issue.

I would also like to have an option to show gizmos for avatar audio when opening the Quick Menu. That way, I can identify where the sounds are on the avatar, and which avatar in specific is playing a particular sound, hiding them accordingly

Yes please. This is such a problem in huge publics that I've just muted avatar audio entirely and never looked back. It's so frustrating having to go into the Instance tab and disable their avatar one by one until you figure out the correct one. Just show me who's making audio and an easy mute button please.
@{5cfb491476b5b77800e860ec|full_name} Turn off Shaders in your safety settings, that's what that's for.

@{68098a4626271974ef4d2775|full_name} Just because community guidelines disallows it doesn't prevent how easily abusable these features are anyway. 

Vrcsdk allows you to displace audio sources and materials as far as the maximum hitbox size, which, with avatar scaling, can be over 250 meters.

One can easily make an avatar that is just a 250 meter wide hitbox full of small  high pitch audio sources, use a material to hide their nameplate, and proceed to spam an instance. A single 16,000 khz squealing tone only uses less than 1kb of memory and can be looped easily. If you want to blow up peoples headphones/speakers you can do a low pass 700hz drone on loop with some mild distortion.

Because nobody knows who this person is, due to their avatar being impossible to see, and said avatar being in the good/excellent range due to having no mesh, armature, and only a handful of audio files, will likely be shown by most people on the default safety settings.

You can basically make avatars specifically designed to blow out peoples eardrums, and nobody is capable of seeing/finding them, because vrchat has no method of finding audio sources.

The existence of saftey settings isn't an excuse to like, not have the ability to not have your ears fucking destroyed on someone else's whim because they have a surface level knowledge of sound design and how the sdk functions.

This would be so helpful. This is one of the number one issues I run into when hosting meets for groups, and is one of the hardest to moderate, because once the audio playback ends, its even harder to figure out who it came from, and even then, that's only if the sound wasn't global. It's not only one of the hardest things to do to find a player responsible for an avi sound, it's also the situation where I've had the most issues of never being able to catch the person who did it, which has meant on multiple occasions, I've had to kind of awkwardly go around to everyone in the instance and be like "Hey, as a reminder, global avi sounds or highly disruptive avi sounds aren't allowed in this group's instances", and apologizing to everyone for not being able to resolve it in a way that is satisfactory. Right now, finding people who pull things like that a lot of the time, can feel like barely more than a witch hunt.

Like if it could just be like a different color of nameplate highlight for avatar sounds, or something like that, it'd be so helpful.

Honestly, extended from this, which I may make a separate feedback suggestion about this also, now that its in my head, if it's possible, if players could make instances that automatically disabled global avatar sounds, sounds that are too loud, or even just disable avi sounds, fully, it would be super helpful. Even more helpful would be is if it were that instance masters and group moderators had the options to toggle them on and off in the instance options our quick menus.
@{699e32a7804d20e970d8e8b1|full_name} Still hoping this one day will get implemented.

details:
I'm sure a lot of us who in here deals with this issue and it's very annoying to track quickly or find out who's avatar is emitting global audio sound or other audio sounds. 

It would be a nice addition to VRC itself, as well as moderation to have a way to find out which users are emitting Avatar Sounds or Global Audio sounds and not having to turn/off every avatar in an instance which can be quite tedious and time consuming. 

Excuse my Microsoft paint Drawing skill, but it would be nice to have it in the 'Instance' Tab, as that's where I and I think most of us look for people talking/playing audio to disrupt other issues, especially when they're hiding in meshes. The blue (Which we already have) shows Voice being transmitted, the red on the right would indicate if an user is emitting Avatar Audio the left when Voice is transmitted.
title: Show if an User is emitting Avatar Sound
